skill.name: creating-issues
skill.description: Helps create GitHub issues that follow project conventions. It validates titles, suggests labels, uses templates, and guides project board metadata.
skill.summary: Create consistent GitHub issues with titles, labels, templates, milestones, and project metadata.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer primarily matched Markdown backticks, command examples, and helper scripts that use fixed argv lists. I found no prompt injection, obfuscation, credential exfiltration, arbitrary shell construction, or unauthorized network callback behavior. GitHub CLI helpers can change repository data, so users should approve mutating commands before execution.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI commands can modify external repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Keep issue creation, project updates, and bulk edits behind explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Future helper changes could introduce command injection if shell strings are added.
remediation.suggestion: Continue using argv lists for subprocess calls and avoid shell=True for all GitHub and Git commands.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when issues have vague titles, missing labels, or weak acceptance criteria. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create complete GitHub issues.
actual_capabilities: Validates issue titles for imperative wording, length, and banned type prefixes.
Recommends type, priority, scope, and branch labels from issue context.
Generates structured issue bodies with summaries, criteria, and supporting context.
Detects scope labels from env.json, branch names, and configured project scopes.
Lists repository labels, milestones, and user projects through GitHub CLI helper scripts.
Prepares issue creation steps that include project boards, milestones, and relationship checks.
limitations: Live GitHub data requires the gh CLI and an authenticated account.
It cannot prove labels, milestones, or projects exist unless helpers query the repository.
Parent-child issue links require a separate relationship management workflow.
Human review is still needed before creating or bulk editing issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare sprint backlog issues
use_cases.description: Create clear issue titles, labels, and acceptance criteria before sprint planning.

use_cases.title: Standardize bug reports
use_cases.description: Turn bug notes into consistent reports with reproduction steps and expected behavior.

use_cases.title: Create implementation tasks
use_cases.description: Break feature work into scoped GitHub issues with priority, milestone, and project guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Check an issue title
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GitHub issue title and suggest a better version: [BUG] Login fails.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a new issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue for improving validation errors in the checkout form.

prompt_templates.title: Select labels and metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend type, priority, scope, milestone, and project board metadata for this issue: Add retry handling to webhook delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan related issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Split a new authentication feature into related GitHub issues with titles, labels, acceptance criteria, and relationship guidance.

output_examples.input: Is this title good: [BUG] Login fails?
output_examples.output: The title uses a type prefix and is too vague. A better title is Fix login authentication failure.

output_examples.input: Create an issue for adding webhook retry handling.
output_examples.output: Suggested type is feature, priority is medium, and scope should match the webhook component. The body should include retry rules and success criteria.

output_examples.input: What should I confirm before creating five issues for a new feature?
output_examples.output: Confirm the project board, milestone, parent-child relationships, affected scope, and priority before creating the issues.

best_practices: Use one type label, one priority label, and at least one scope label for every issue.
Ask for project board, milestone, and relationship details before creating complex issue sets.
Write acceptance criteria that define observable completion and verification steps.
anti_patterns: Do not put type prefixes like bug or feature in issue titles.
Do not create issues without a scope label unless the user explicitly confirms it.
Do not use task lists as a substitute for true parent-child issue relationships.

faq.question: Does this skill create GitHub issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can prepare commands and helper steps. Users should approve any action that changes GitHub data.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: GitHub CLI is required for helper scripts that list labels, milestones, projects, or create issues.

faq.question: Can it choose labels for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends type, priority, scope, and optional branch labels from the issue context.

faq.question: Can it manage parent-child issue links?
faq.answer: It explains when links are needed, but true parent-child links require a separate relationship workflow.

faq.question: Can I use custom templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes standard, bug report, and feature request template files that can be adapted.
